label: Luke 17:1
text:
He said to the disciples,
“It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!

label: Luke 17:2
text: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.

label: Luke 17:3
text: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.

label: Luke 17:4
text: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”

label: Luke 17:5
text: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”

label: Luke 17:6
text:
The Lord said,
“If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.

label: Luke 17:7
text: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say, when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table,’

label: Luke 17:8
text: and will not rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me, while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?

label: Luke 17:9
text: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.

label: Luke 17:10
text: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”

label: Luke 17:11
text: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.

label: Luke 17:12
text: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.

label: Luke 17:13
text: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

label: Luke 17:14
text:
When he saw them, he said to them,
“Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.

label: Luke 17:15
text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.

label: Luke 17:16
text: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.

label: Luke 17:17
text:
Jesus answered,
“Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?

label: Luke 17:18
text: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?”

label: Luke 17:19
text:
Then he said to him,
“Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”

label: Luke 17:20
text:
Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them,
“God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;

label: Luke 17:21
text: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”

label: Luke 17:22
text:
He said to the disciples,
“The days will come, when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.

label: Luke 17:23
text: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away, nor follow after them,

label: Luke 17:24
text: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of the one part under the sky, shines to the other part under the sky; so will the Son of Man be in his day.

label: Luke 17:25
text: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

label: Luke 17:26
text: As it was in the days of Noah, even so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.

label: Luke 17:27
text: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.

label: Luke 17:28
text: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;

label: Luke 17:29
text: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky, and destroyed them all.

label: Luke 17:30
text: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.

label: Luke 17:31
text: In that day, he who will be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.

label: Luke 17:32
text: Remember Lot’s wife!

label: Luke 17:33
text: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.

label: Luke 17:34
text: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. The one will be taken, and the other will be left.

label: Luke 17:35
text: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left.”

variants.reading: the whole verse is absent (the KJV text 'Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left' is a repetition of Matthew 24:40)

label: Luke 17:37
text:
They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?”
He said to them,
“Where the body is, there will the vultures also be gathered together.”

label: Forgive a repentant brother seven times in a day
statement: If a brother sins against you and repents, forgive him - even seven times in a day.

label: The sycamore tree (Ficus sycomorus) in Palestine
statement: The sycamore (sykomorea, Ficus sycomorus) was a tree known in first-century Palestine.

label: A slave plows, shepherds, and serves supper first
statement: A slave plowed the field or kept sheep and, coming in from the field, prepared and served his master's meal before he ate himself.

label: The border route between Samaria and Galilee to Jerusalem
statement: On the way to Jerusalem he passed along the borders of Samaria and Galilee - the road Galileans took going up to Jerusalem.

label: Ten leprous men met him, standing at a distance
statement: As he entered a village, ten leprous men met him and stood at a distance, raising their voices for mercy.

label: Cleansed lepers show themselves to the priests
statement: A cleansed leper was to show himself to the priest, the examination and cleansing prescribed in Leviticus 14.

label: The ten were cleansed as they went
statement: As the ten lepers went to the priests, they were cleansed.

label: The thankful one was a Samaritan, a stranger
statement: The one who turned back to glorify God at Jesus' feet was a Samaritan - a stranger to Judeans.

label: The days of Noah: the flood remembered as judgment
statement: In the days of Noah people ate, drank and married until the day Noah entered the ark and the flood came and destroyed them all - remembered as a sudden divine judgment.

label: The days of Lot: fire from heaven on Sodom
statement: In the days of Lot they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted and built; on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulfur rained from the sky and destroyed them all.
